contract: CBWeb3 Scenario B — Hub-and-spoke settlement (circuit breaker, transfer limits, oversight disclosure)

vectors.title: Create a daily transfer limit — human decimal in, wei out
vectors.description: A Central Bank caps a participant's daily outflow. The same logical field changes unit between request and response.

preconditions.session: cookie carrying the central_bank realm role

vectors.notes: COMPOUNDING UNIT TRAP. max_amount is a HUMAN DECIMAL on input ('100000.00') and WEI on output ('100000000000000000000000'), under the same field name. A client that reads a limit and writes it back unchanged shrinks it by 10^18. An empty participant_id means 'all participants on this spoke'; an empty currency means 'all currencies'. Only max_amount is required.

vectors.title: List the limits this Central Bank created
vectors.description: Scoped to the authenticated Central Bank. There is no network-wide view.
vectors.notes: Every max_amount in this list is in wei — see limits-hp-01.

vectors.title: Delete a limit — 204 with no body
vectors.description: The only 204 in the entire published Toolbox surface.
vectors.notes: Assert there is no response body. A client that unconditionally parses JSON on a 2xx will throw here.

vectors.title: A max_amount that is not a decimal is 422, not 400
vectors.description: The canonical malformed-amount assertion for Scenario B: the request shape is valid, the value is not.
vectors.notes: 422 for an unparseable value, 400 only for a malformed body or an absent max_amount. This is one of the few places on the platform where the 400/422 distinction is drawn deliberately and documented upstream.

vectors.title: Deleting another Central Bank's limit is 422, not 403
vectors.description: The limit exists but cannot be deleted by this caller. The platform expresses that as unprocessable rather than forbidden.

preconditions.session: central_bank cookie for Central Bank A

vectors.notes: A limit id that does not exist at all is 404 on the same route. The 403 declared on this operation is the role gate, not the ownership check — three distinct refusals, three different codes.

vectors.title: Pause a pair 1-of-N — a request body the platform declares nowhere
vectors.description: Any single Central Bank can halt a pair. Resuming takes two.
vectors.notes: The platform document declares NO requestBody at all for this operation, yet all three fields are required. A client built from the upstream document literally cannot operate the circuit breaker. The contract publishes the body under x-cbweb3-source: implementation-observed. reason_code is stored verbatim and the platform declares no vocabulary for it, so none is published.

vectors.title: Propose a resume (2-of-N step 1)
vectors.description: Returns a request_id that the second Central Bank must sign.
vectors.notes: Also declared with no requestBody upstream. Note this handler does NOT check for a missing pair or bank_id up front, so an incomplete body fails as 422 rather than 400 — the opposite of pause.

vectors.title: Sign the resume — the second Central Bank executes it
vectors.description: Two Central Banks are required, so the signer must not be the proposer. On execution the breaker returns to LIVE.

preconditions.session: central_bank cookie for a DIFFERENT Central Bank than the proposer

vectors.notes: Confirm with GET /api/v2/governance/circuit-breaker/status that trading actually resumed — see breaker-edge-01 for why the 200 alone is not enough.

vectors.title: Pause without reason_code is 400
vectors.description: All three fields are checked up front by the pause handler, unlike the resume-request handler.
vectors.notes: Undeclared upstream, since the platform document declares neither the body nor this status. Published in the contract under x-cbweb3-source: implementation-observed.

vectors.title: A disputed resume signature is 422 CIRCUIT_BREAKER_RESUME_DISPUTED
vectors.description: The one circuit-breaker failure that carries a machine-readable error_code.
vectors.notes: Undeclared upstream. Every other circuit-breaker failure returns a bare {error}, so this is the only one a client can branch on programmatically.

vectors.title: A 200 on resume-sign does NOT mean trading resumed
vectors.description: The signature was recorded but the resume did not execute — quorum is not yet met, or execution failed. The breaker is still not LIVE.
vectors.notes: BRANCH ON state, NOT ON THE STATUS CODE. state LIVE means the resume executed; state RESUME_PENDING on the same 200 means it did not, and swaps on the pair will still fail with 422 CIRCUIT_BREAKER_HALTED. Note also that pause_initiator and pause_reason on the status endpoint are only present in the LOCAL projection — a pause raised on another gateway is visible as state but not as attribution.

vectors.title: Open a Master Viewing Key disclosure request
vectors.description: Supervisory disclosure of a private transaction, gated by a two-signature quorum and a 72-hour expiry.
vectors.notes: 200, not 201, despite creating a record. TWO FIELDS ARE RENAMED between request and record: requestor_id becomes requested_by_bank_id and tx_ref becomes target_transaction_ref. requestor_id is taken from the BODY and is not cross-checked against the session — unlike everywhere else on this platform. reason_code is stored verbatim and validated against nothing. tx_ref is unconstrained in form; note that the compliance surface elsewhere describes an HTLC contract id as 0x-prefixed hex while every HTLC endpoint uses the htlc-a1b2c3d4 form, so a third identifier convention is in play here.

vectors.title: Sign a disclosure request — the acknowledgement tells you nothing
vectors.description: Records one signature. The response is a fixed acknowledgement that does not report whether quorum was reached.
vectors.notes: Re-read GET /api/v2/oversight/disclosure-status/{requestID} afterwards to learn the real outcome — this response is a fixed literal and carries no state. A second signature from the SAME signer_id is rejected, so the quorum is genuinely two distinct authorities.

vectors.title: Read disclosure status — public, mixed-case path placeholder
vectors.description: Unauthenticated read of the request record. Note the path placeholder is requestID in mixed case, unlike every other identifier on this surface.
vectors.notes: The delivered state vocabulary is PENDING, QUORUM_REACHED, APPROVED, EXPIRED, REJECTED. Signing after expires_at (72 hours after opened_at) fails and transitions the request to EXPIRED. closed_at appears only once quorum is reached.

vectors.title: Signing an expired or already-signed request is 422
vectors.description: One 422 covers four distinct conditions: unknown request, request not PENDING, request expired, or this signer_id has already signed.
vectors.notes: Undeclared upstream. A client cannot tell the four conditions apart from the status code, and the error text is free-form, so re-read the status endpoint to decide what to do.

vectors.title: An unknown disclosure request id is 404
vectors.description: Unlike the sign route, the public status route does distinguish a missing record.
vectors.notes: An EMPTY identifier is 400 rather than 404 on the same route.

vectors.title: Sovereign liquidity top-up — omitting is_token_a means side B
vectors.description: A Central Bank adds to its own side of a sovereign pair. The side selector defaults in a way that silently picks the other side.

preconditions.session: cookie or bearer for a Central Bank

vectors.notes: 201, not 200. ALWAYS send is_token_a explicitly: omitting it does not mean 'unspecified', it means side B. Assert the returned side matches your intent. A pair the gateway does not classify as sovereign yields 422 NOT_SOVEREIGN_PAIR; an insufficient balance yields 422 INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE; a gateway with the feature unwired yields 501, which is a deployment-shape skip rather than a failure. The contract's example pair_id here is a third naming convention (W-BRL-ARS) — do not copy it, take the value from listPairs.
